evidence:
Source-only Pass within the available local portfolio. The actual frozen workbook was opened using openpyxl: Quality Checks!row 54 and Internal Quality Checks!row 54 both define check 53 as reading as authored for this product, fitting the suite domain plan, and not being a nouns-swapped sibling. The frozen skill reference, quality-checks.md:212-214, specifically requires comparison of sibling names/concepts and defines the defect as the same flows and criteria with renamed entities. Shared infrastructure and components are expressly permitted by NEW_TASK_AUTHORING_CONTEXT.md:203; task-specific domain behavior must differ.

The product has a coherent devtools identity rather than generic CRUD naming. Frozen task instruction.md:1 asks to write JavaScript, HTML or CSS and see results beside the editor; :3 asks for last-good preview recovery and safe concurrent saves. task.toml:5-15 consistently identifies Colderwater Playground, code-playground/devtools keywords, isolation/cancellation/recovery difficulty, and the disclosed provenance 'Adapted from the supplied Colderwater playground task.' This is declared adaptation, not a claim of wholly novel provenance. The snapshot directory named task is an infrastructure wrapper, not evidence of an identity mismatch. environment/assets/seed_data.json:2-4 identifies Colderwater and an empty snippet collection, not renamed commerce/report data.

All six public notes were examined. Product-specific rules include fresh JS/HTML execution, CSS over an inert last-successful document, cancelled callbacks never becoming current, a shared five-second execution budget, last-good preview restoration, full-document HTML source line numbers and expandable console values (environment/instructions/behaviour.md:5-21). The snippet origin/network boundary and separate unsupported execution families are explicit (security.md:3-11); overview.md:5-9 separates filename-driven execution, library records and app examples. These rules demand an actual execution workbench beyond a text editor or CRUD library. The task permits tool/layout choices (integration.md:3 and policy.md:5), supporting authored outcomes rather than a canned implementation prescription.

The 58 parsed Functional outcomes are specific to these flows: tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:50,57,78 and 85 cover language/CSS behavior; :106-120 cover supersession, Stop and rollback; :127-162 cover origin/network boundaries, refusal and loop timeouts; :169-246 cover JS/HTML/timer/Promise error messages, user-source lines and restoration; :253-309 cover console/Auto-run; :337-400 cover exact durable snippets and stale-save/title rules. The corresponding scenario headings and execution probes were inspected in functional/prompt.md, including S02, S04, S05, S08 and S09. Render requires an actually authored marker in preview and console (gates/render/judge.toml:25), and Constraints requires a newly saved snippet retrieved by a clean visitor (gates/constraints/judge.toml:25-27). All five prompt identities and all five criterion files were checked for product framing. Polish and Visual discuss the editor/preview/console/library, not an unrelated sibling. Reference source corroborates the authored concept: solution/app/src/runtime.ts:124-161 builds filename-selected execution documents, :164-202 implements preview lifecycle and rollback; app.tsx:147-155 renders Colderwater, its editor and conflict-recovery UI. Starter README.md:4-16 distinguishes runnable examples, a deliberate error, an infinite loop and filename dispatch. These reads establish task identity, not universal runtime correctness.

Local comparison covered the first substantive product paragraph in all 38 projects/**/instruction.md files outside environment/, including the current Colderwater source and the template. The closest concepts were examined more deeply. PatchPad is an incident-report editor (projects/patchpad-editor-v3/instruction.md:1-5); its overview.md:33-35 requires a custom editor and forbids ready-made editors, and editing.md:23-52 centers on graphemes, selection, clipboard, multi-caret and Undo/Redo. Its 29 Functional criteria center on those operations and revision history. Colderwater shares legitimate concurrent-save/restart patterns but its execution, isolation, console and recovery flows are materially different. GridForge's instruction.md describes a shared spreadsheet, and its 36 Functional descriptions center on cells/formulas, references, ranges, presence and workbook history. Read-only TOML comparison found zero exact Functional description matches between Colderwater's 58 criteria and either sibling; this supports the semantic comparison but is not by itself proof against paraphrased copying. A targeted scan of the frozen authored text/source for Patchpad, Gridforge, Ridgeline, BazaarBridge, CHANGE_ME, TODO, lorem ipsum, incident report, spreadsheet, checkout and invoice produced no matches (rg exit 1). Common shared harness and generic visual vocabulary are not treated as plagiarism.

Scope limits: available local tasks and documented authoring guidance support suite fit; no external/global corpus, assignment registry or source-originality investigation was available or claimed. Colderwater's current source, frozen snapshot, archives and prior candidate copies are the same task's history, not distinct sibling plagiarism witnesses. No previous per-row findings or reviewer verdict reports were consulted. No live app, Docker, paid judge, Oracle or target-model run was performed for this row, and no runtime or hosted-clearance conclusion follows from this source judgment.
counterexample: False-fail witness: a conforming Colderwater implementation may reuse the shared staged harness, a standard editor component, the stale-save/restart pattern also present in PatchPad, or the supplied Colderwater predecessor. Its snippet execution/isolation/cancellation/rollback/console flows remain distinct. Counting that shared infrastructure or copies of the same product as plagiarism would falsely fail it. False-pass witness: rename PatchPad's actual incident-report product and criteria to Colderwater while retaining its custom text selection, multi-caret and report-history flows, with no execution runtime or console. The brand/devtools labels alone would superficially look authored, but it would lack the actual frozen requirements at behaviour.md:5-21 and the corresponding language/cancellation/error criteria. The reviewed candidate instead has those concrete domain-specific requirements and implementation paths. These are source-level adversarial comparisons, not executed app mutations.
